newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open unchanged to 0.05 cent per lb weaker on Wednesday, dealers said.

The market is expected to maintain its recent trading range ahead of the Independence Day holiday on Friday. Nearby resistance in benchmark October was pegged at Tuesday's high of 11.40 cents, followed by 11.50 cents.
Support was seen at 11.20 cents basis the October contract.

Traders said the retreat from the highs made early on Tuesday could signal a move towards the lower end of the trading range. The October contract closed 0.05 cent firmer at 11.24 cents per lb on Tuesday, after trading from a contract high of 11.40 cents, to 11.21 cents.
The rest of the board settled 0.06 to 0.10 cent higher, having climbed to new contract highs during the day.

LIFFE white sugar futures were weaker in thin trade Wednesday in slow and rangebound trade. At 0850 EDT/1250 GMT, the spot August contract stood down $0.70 at $321.20, while the rest of the board was trading $0.10 to $0.40 weaker.
